A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SSLogic research. Their full text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated prompt templates and renumbered analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original RL training results, controlled Seed/Evolve comparisons, difficulty and code-complexity analyses, and pipeline diagnostics.

after.justification: v2 retains these results and adds external Enigmata training experiments, KORBench evaluation, token-budget analyses, and a human audit.

M1.justification: The CKPro agent hierarchy, generator–validator evolution, consensus verification, blind review, and refinement loop are retained. The executable prompt templates and training procedure are unchanged; revised checker and solver descriptions clarify the existing method.

E1.justification: v2 adds evolution and training on 30 external English-only Enigmata puzzle types, extending beyond the original Chinese seed distribution; Enigmata previously served as an evaluation benchmark. It also adds KORBench evaluation across five reasoning categories. Removed benchmark mentions lack corresponding v1 results, so they do not establish dropped evaluations.

E2.justification: The Seed/Evolve controls, mathematical-data mixtures, ARC mixture, and Qwen3 baselines are retained. The new Enigmata experiment extends the same Seed/Evolve comparison to another dataset; GPT-5.4 serves as a synthesis backend, not a competing baseline.

E3.justification: v2 introduces token-matched comparisons, nearly size-matched Enigmata training, length-normalized reflection measurements, and a human-audit protocol. Appendix B also replaces v1's mathematics pass@64/pass@8 specifications with pass@1 estimated using 64/8 samples. This substantially revises reported evaluation settings, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses examine compute-budget confounding, reflection frequency after length normalization, category-selective KORBench/BBH gains, and failures in 100 human-audited task families. These materially extend the retained subsampling, difficulty, complexity, and pipeline analyses. A gate-by-gate training ablation remains absent.

E5.justification: Appendix I retains the same 2,000-iteration bootstrap analysis and 95% confidence intervals. v2 adds no training-seed replication information, significance testing, or uncertainty-estimation procedure; the new benchmark and audit results are point estimates.

E6.justification: Original Table 2 numerical entries are retained. New results include Enigmata-trained BBH scores of 61.8 versus 67.3, KORBench overall scores of 43.0 versus 51.0, token-matched macro accuracy of 0.2312 versus 0.2480, and 85/100 audited families deemed usable. The new BBH breakdown in Section 5.3 reports 59.4 versus 69.3 without reconciling these figures with Table 2.

T1.justification: Task-family definitions, unique-answer assumptions, gating and consensus mathematics, the pass@k estimator, and the KL formula remain substantively unchanged. Revised indices, state arguments, and complexity symbols clarify notation; no new theorem, proof, or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The central task-family synthesis contribution is retained. The abstract and conclusion extend the training-utility claim to token-matched and external-seed settings and highlight category-selective improvements. Section 6 additionally makes an explicit near-thousand-family novelty claim.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the explanation that complexity forces System 2 behavior with a selective-gains hypothesis and acknowledges limits of AST-based novelty measures. New limitations and audit discussion address seed dependence, restricted model coverage, missing gate ablations, survivorship bias, and prompt–code mismatches. Appendix N attributes roughly half the step-matched advantage to additional tokens.

D1.justification: Appendix M documents the new experiment's GPT-5.4 backend, two refinement iterations, difficulty levels, instance counts, and reuse of existing training hyperparameters. Appendices L/N document audit inputs and token-log comparisons. Core implementation details and prompts remain intact; the conclusion now explicitly states release of both framework and datasets.

R1.justification: v2 adds 'ARC is a vision problem!', replaces the Reinforce++ citation with OpenRLHF, and removes CRUXEval. Related work adds limited novelty and verification-focused positioning. Numerous other bibliography edits concern the same works' authorship or publication metadata.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites affect the abstract, conclusion, validation description, and mechanism discussion, alongside terminology cleanup and additional cross-references. New limitations, impact, and experimental sections extend the existing organization; most established sections and prompt appendices remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the displays with token-budget and efficiency plots, KORBench and audit tables, and an Enigmata block in Table 2. It redesigns the overview and evaluation-metric table and merges the former complexity-distribution and pattern-coverage figures. Some appendix plots redisplay existing analyses rather than add evidence.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens assessment of the central training-utility claim through external English-seed experiments and token-matched controls, addressing limitations of v1's step-matched, original-seed evidence. The human audit and explicit limitations also make reliability and applicability more assessable. Unreconciled BBH figures and the absence of fully compute-matched and gate-ablation experiments remain concerns, but the added controls and candid failure analysis provide a substantial net improvement.
